correctness.rationale: The Heawood graph has 14 cubic vertices, 21 edges, and is the Fano-plane point-line incidence graph. A rotation system assigns one of two cyclic orders at each cubic vertex (2^14 cases). Facial walks are cycles of sigma composed with dart reversal; counting faces, one face yields genus 4 from V-E+F=-6. I built an independent exhaustive 14-bit rotation tracer, independently enumerated all 336 graph automorphisms by adjacency-preserving graph isomorphisms (rather than the source’s GL(3,2) coordinatization), and enumerated orbits/mirror reversal. My full census yielded face histogram {1:4480,3:10880,5:1008,7:16}; one-face orbits {336:12,112:4}; mirror-pair sizes {672:6,224:2}. Exhaustion genuinely covers the complete finite universe; does not extrapolate to arbitrary graphs or metric cut loci.
residual_risks: The complete finite 2^14 case census was independently enumerated; metric geometries beyond these ribbon rotations are outside scope.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical 3-regular highly symmetric Fano incidence graph, making maximal-genus one-face rotation systems a natural finite topological object. Its complete labeled counts and symmetry classes classify its orientable one-boundary ribbon neighborhoods and hence the corresponding combinatorial cut-locus strip types. Although finite and computational, this is full exact classification of a natural object, not a random small sample.
residual_risks: Relevance is to the precisely stated natural invariant and family; no assertion of broader applications, robustness or generalization beyond this source claim.

final_claim: Exactly 4480 of the 16384 oriented local rotation systems of the Heawood graph are one-face genus-4 systems, with 16 orbits under the full graph automorphism group of order 336 (12 orbits of 336 and 4 of 112), paired by global mirror reversal into 8 unoriented types.
